strengths: Using reranking+ majority voting to choose solution and compare different re-ranking algorithm, different model size.
This work propose the multi-tasks tuning in a sequential manner while a new training object.
Experiments (Table 3) show consistent improvement by __RR.Top-8__ compared with __RR.All__.
Improvement of the sequential fine-tuning over the MLE fine-tuning.
Investigate a number of re-ranking strategy to show the advantages of reranking through top-_K_ clusters.
The solution-cluster re-ranking approach creatively combines majority voting and re-ranking in a novel way to improve performance.
weaknesses: I find its novelty is limited. Both reranking and majority-voting are not new, it seems the authors just combine them in this paper.
Multi-task sequential fine-tuning is one of major contribution. However, I find it increase performance very limited as shown in Table 4.

The paper claims the method obtains an 11.2% accuracy improvement. However, the simply SFT on PRM800+MATH already has about 7.6% gain as shown in Table2 (47.6->55.2), so the biggest gain is from SFT instead of proposed method.
The paper only reports the performance on PaLM2. I think the authors can report the method on other LLM, like llama.
In sec 5.1, I am not sure what's the dataset GSM800K? maybe it is PRM800K. The authors should carefully check the paper writing.
The contribution is incremental to the research community.
The absolute improvements are not really significant for both solution reranking and sequential fine-tuning (Table 3 and 4).
It could be unnecessary to make this approach general for everyone.

I would expect some deeper insights besides the engineering efforts made in this work. For example, how does the sequential fine-tuning change the behavior of the models? Answering some scientific questions like this would give the readers more insights for future research.
For reranking, why K is 8? I think there should be more experiments to explain.
One more dataset would be even more convincing.
Writing needs to be improved, with specific concerns about unclear handling of pair loss, unbalanced sampling, and use of gold annotations in re-ranking.
Lack of comparison with other open-source LLMs.
Lack of comparison with other powerful LLMs such as ChatGPT [1], GPT-4 [2], and Claude-2 [3].
The experiments are solely conducted on PaLM 2 models, not demonstrating generalizability to other model families such as LLaMA [4].
Compared to the baseline, the performance gain is minimal.
